h: Toboggans, treetops and the heart of the island
p: Robin Hill sits near Arreton, just outside Newport, right in the middle of the island. That central spot makes it an easy trip wherever you're staying, whether that's Ryde, Sandown, Shanklin or Cowes.

One of the big favourites here is the toboggan run, where you whizz down the hillside on a track. Kids and grown-ups both love it, so expect to go back for another go. There's also plenty for younger children, from play areas to trails through the woods, so families with a range of ages can all find something.

Robin Hill is no stranger to big events. It hosted the Bestival music festival for many years, and these days it's known for its seasonal events, including after-dark light trails through the woods in some seasons. Check what's on before you go, as the events calendar changes through the year.

Allow a full day if you want to make the most of it. Wear comfortable shoes, as the site is spread over hills and woodland, and pack a picnic if the weather's good. On rainy days, the indoor play area comes into its own.

The park is run by the same family company that runs Blackgang Chine, so if you're on the island for a few days, it's easy to plan a visit to both. Nearby, Arreton Barns has craft shops, a pub and a little church to explore. Carisbrooke Castle, with its donkeys and its links to Charles I, is just the other side of Newport, and Osborne, Queen Victoria's island home, is a short drive north at East Cowes.
